Arch Linux and the myth of 'The Arch Way'

Haha, I remember the AIF! I remember when they removed it back in like 2009 or 2012 or so... I was sooo ticked. Not because I couldn't install Arch by hand, just because it made no sense to. It's long, it's tedious, it's easy to screw something up if you don't already know the process, etc.

Antergos, and other 'installers' were a great thing for Arch and allowed me to install it on many machines quickly so I could just get the system running.

For me, it's the uphill climb that makes Arch what it is. It forces you to learn about the way it installs, it makes you make decisions about what you're installing, and it gives you a sense of accomplishment in doing it for yourself.

By using an installer, you're no more prepared to fix issues than if you had installed Ubuntu, or Linux Mint... and issues will arise, by nature of being a rolling release distro.

So you can call it "purism," but I call it "preparedness." Yes, installers are nice for when you're creating a boatload of Arch machines, but that's really what scripting is for.

Case in point: if you use an installer, and put a GUI on Arch, do you know what startx does? Do you know that you have xorg on your machine? Do you know how to enable/disable auto-login to get into your GUI without ever having to see the command line?

Sure, some people will know all of these things, but most will not. Most think Arch in this holy Grail, and they're looking to achieve a status without putting in the time/effort. So the forums get flooded with "my desktop won't start" and "what is an Xorg log?" This is where the Arch community loses their patience, and you get a ton of "RTFM" responses... they've obviously taken a shortcut, and avoided the manual thusfar, nobetter time to start referencing the manual than now!

So, no, you cannot "run Arch" with an installer... because "running Arch" is more than using a keyboard and mouse with the OS... it's about knowing/understanding how it works, why it works, and where to go when it no longer works.
